_readme: Structure layouts for DBSIM.EXE's simulation objects, applied to the Ghidra project by
ES2ApplyStructures.java (tools/ghidra_scripts/). Re-run that script after adding entries here --
it is idempotent.
Third of three files. known_symbols.json owns address->function findings; known_vtables.json owns
which vtable slot means what; this file owns FIELD LAYOUT -- offset, width and meaning inside an
object. A field offset is recorded once here rather than once per doc that happens to read it.
Per struct definition:
name        - Ghidra data-type name, created under category /ES2.
binary      - 'VSHELL' or 'DBSIM' (must match the -process file name at apply time).
size        - total length in bytes. THIS IS A FINDING, NOT THE HIGHEST OFFSET ANYONE HAS
DOCUMENTED. See 'Sizes' below.
vtable      - OPTIONAL, the known_vtables.json type the field at offset 0 points to.
description - what the class is; becomes the data type's description.
notes       - OPTIONAL, things known about the layout that are not placeable fields: a
sub-object whose extent is still open, a codegen idiom that makes a field hard to
find, a disagreement between two docs.
fields      - sparse, in offset order. Each has:
offset      - byte offset from the start of the struct.
width       - byte width. Checked against the resolved data type's own length;
a mismatch is an error, not a coercion.
type        - 'byte', 'sbyte', 'short', 'ushort', 'int', 'uint', 'void *',
'undefined1|2|4', '<Name> *' for a pointer to a named type,
'<Name>[n]' for an array, or '<Name>' for a struct defined
earlier in this file or already present under /ES2.
name        - OMITTED for 'low' confidence, so a guess can never look like a
confirmed field. 'medium' names carry a 'maybe_' prefix. An
unnamed field still earns its place: it pins the WIDTH, which is
what stops the decompiler swallowing its neighbours.
confidence  - 'high' | 'medium' | 'low', same guide as known_symbols.json.
description - evidence: which instruction settled the width, which function
reads or writes it.
WIDTH IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD. A wrong name is a nuisance; a wrong width makes the decompiler
lie in every function that touches the object, and it lies plausibly. Only record a width the
access instruction pins -- MOV byte ptr / MOVSX EAX, word ptr / MOV EAX, dword ptr. Where two
readers disagree, that is a finding: leave the field out and say so in 'notes'. Never average.
ES2ApplyStructures checks the declared width against the resolved type's own length, refuses a
field that overlaps its neighbour, and refuses one that runs past the declared size. Widen the
schema rather than working around those checks.
DEFINITION ORDER MATTERS WITHIN 'structs'. A field naming another struct resolves only against
types defined EARLIER in this array (or already present under /ES2), so a sub-object goes above
the class that embeds it.
SIZES. Every one here comes from the free-list pool the class is allocated from, not from the
highest documented offset. Pool_Init (004719cc) takes (pool, count, elementSize) and the allocator
(00471a24) hands back node+8, so the element size is the object's true length: mech 0x36a from
00425185, flyer 0x291 from 00425220, structure 0x26d from 00405e1e. SimObject itself is never
allocated alone; its length is bounded above by where the derived classes start their own fields
-- 0x1f2 for both the mech and the structure, 0x1fa for the flyer.
INHERITANCE IS EMBEDDING. A derived class embeds its base at offset 0 rather than restating the
base's fields, so one recorded fact serves every class that has it.
APPLICATIONS. Defining a struct renders nothing on its own: a function's parameter has to be typed
with it. Each entry names a function (by address, so a rename cannot break it), the zero-based
parameter index, and the struct to point that parameter at. Only list a parameter whose type was
read out of the function, not assumed from its name.
A function that carries a 'signature' in known_symbols.json owns its whole parameter list there,
struct types included -- do not list its parameters here as well. Applying a signature replaces
the parameter list, so two files describing one parameter would fight. ES2ApplySymbolNames keeps
a parameter typed with a pointer into /ES2 across a signature apply and WARNs when the two
disagree, which is how you find out you have written the fact down twice.
RUN ORDER only matters on a database that has never had these files applied: a signature naming a
struct type cannot resolve until that type exists, so the structures go first. Once the /ES2 types
are in the project they stay there, and from then on any of the three scripts can be run alone, in
any order, as often as you like. After a fresh import run tools/scripts/ghidra_apply_all.sh, which
does all three in the right order; after that, run whichever one you need directly.

structs.name: Transform32
structs.description: The engine's 32-byte transform: a 3x3 Q14 rotation matrix, a rank byte that says how much of it is meaningful, and an int32 translation. Every object keeps one, every hit test composes one, and Transform_Concat (0047f914) branches on the rank byte to skip the work a translation-only or Z-only frame does not need.

fields.name: m
fields.description: Row-major 3x3, Q14. Written by BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 (0047eaac), read by Transform_ApplyToPoint (00480330) and Transform_ApplyToShortPoint (004800c8).

fields.name: rank
fields.description: +0x12 -- translation-only / Z-rotation-only / full 3x3. An optimisation switch in Transform_Concat, not a behavioural difference.
+0x13 -- sits between the rank byte and the int32 translation. No reader or writer located; recorded to pin where x starts, not because it is established as padding.

fields.name: x
fields.description: +0x14. Transform_Concat and both Transform_ApplyTo* treat +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c as the translation.

structs.name: CountdownTimer
structs.description: The 3-byte packed countdown record Math_CountdownTimerTick (00467944) steps. THE COUNTER IS THE SHORT AT +1, NOT AT +0 -- verified across all 40 call sites. Records sit in stride-3 runs, so a base whose sibling code reads a short one byte higher is one of these.

fields.description: +0x0 -- untouched by Math_CountdownTimerTick, and for all four global instances (004a9be8, 004a9bec, 004a9ee6, 004a9ee9) never read or written anywhere in DBSIM, only address-taken. Meaning OPEN, not settled as padding.

fields.name: counter
fields.description: +0x1 -- decremented by SimTickDelta and clamped at 0; the tick returns its new value in AX. Every reload site writes this short, not the record base.

structs.name: LongCountdownTimer
structs.description: The engine's second countdown record, stepped by Timer_CountDown (004679a4): the same byte-then-counter shape as CountdownTimer but with an int counter, so it holds a window longer than a short can carry. Which of the two a field is cannot be read off the field itself -- it is settled by which function ticks it. BehaviourBlock +0x04 is one of these (Timer_CountDown is called on mech+0x51, and the block starts at mech+0x4d).

fields.description: +0x00 -- Timer_CountDown is handed this address and works on +0x01, so the byte here is never touched by the tick. No reader or writer located; recorded to pin where the counter starts.

fields.name: counter
fields.description: +0x01 -- milliseconds remaining. Timer_CountDown subtracts SimTickDelta and clamps at 0. The unaligned offset is the whole reason this record has a spare byte in front of it.

structs.name: BehaviourBlock
structs.description: The AI behaviour state a machine currently holds -- 0x45 bytes embedded in the object at +0x4d, not a pointer field. Behaviour_SetState (00413e50) is the only writer, and its 30 call sites are the state machine's edge list. Both Mech_Constructor and Flyer_Constructor hand it obj+0x4d, so it is a base member rather than a mech one.

fields.name: descriptor
fields.description: +0x00 -- the state descriptor installed by Behaviour_SetState. The three dispatcher vtable slots read a triple out of it and return 0 without calling when that triple is entirely zero.

fields.name: dwellTimer
fields.description: +0x04 -- the state's dwell countdown, stepped by Timer_CountDown(mech+0x51); docs cite its counter as mech+0x52, which is this record's own +0x01. Behaviour_SetState does not touch the leading byte. The counter is loaded as descriptor+0x04 plus a 0-15 ms jitter (DAT_004a9bf4 stepped by 13 per state change and masked to 4 bits, so deterministic in call order rather than random). Only eight states actually step it; for the rest it is loaded and never expires.

fields.name: tickCount
fields.description: +0x09 -- zeroed on a state change, incremented once per AI tick by 00413eb0.
+0x0d -- 0x28 bytes zeroed on a state change. Contents not established.
+0x35 -- 0x10 bytes zeroed on a state change, after which +0x36 is set to 1. Contents not established.

structs.name: SimObject
structs.description: The base every object the simulation ticks derives from -- mech, flyer and structure. Its extent is bounded above by where the derived classes start their own fields: 0x1f2 for the mech (Mech_Constructor's HERCS.DAT record store) and the structure (Base_Construct's BASES.DAT record store), 0x1fa for the flyer. Below that boundary the three constructors write an identical block, which is what identifies the layout as shared rather than coincidental.
notes: THE FLAG BLOCK IS ADDRESSED THROUGH obj+0x92. Every reader of the bytes from 0x92 up materialises that address first -- 'LEA ECX,[EBX + 0x92]' -- and then uses a small displacement off it: TargetSelect_CanTarget reads destroyed as [EDX + 0x7] and Mech_Constructor writes 0xa7 as [EAX + 0x15]. So a scalar search for 0x95, 0x99, 0xa1, 0xa5 or 0xa7 returns ZERO sites across the whole binary, and that is not evidence the field is unused. Whether obj+0x92 is a sub-object in the source or just a base register the compiler chose is not settled, so the fields are placed at their absolute offsets here rather than inside an invented struct.

+0x1a4 (a machine's selected target) FALLS INSIDE THIS STRUCT'S EXTENT but is documented as mech+0x1a4 and is not known to be written by any other class. Left out until a flyer or a structure is seen to touch it.

+0x99, +0xa4 and +0xa5 ARE THE 'OUT OF THE FIGHT' TRIPLE, and they are three different conditions rather than three damage latches: destroyed, cannot move, cannot shoot. Each has its own writers and none of them is 'removed from the simulation' -- that is 'Removed', a separate concept the engine models on its own. Which tests read which subset is the behaviour: the detection sweep, the player's target selection and the mission group's condition tier read +0x99 and +0xa4 only; the AI's own tests add +0xa5.

fields.name: vtbl
fields.description: The class vtable -- SimObjectBaseVtable (0049a54c) for a structure, MechVtable (0049a282) for a mech, 0049a5e0 for a flyer. Typing this is what makes an indirect call render as a named method.

fields.name: eulerAngles
fields.description: +0xc -- the object's orientation as three binary angles, and the input BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 turns into 'frame'. Zeroed by SimObjectBase_Constructor (00402188); Flyer_Constructor passes it as the source when it seeds the matrix itself.

fields.name: frame
fields.description: +0x12 -- the shape-to-world frame. SimObject_InstallModelTransform (00401fe4) builds it from eulerAngles when 'frameValid' is clear. ITS TRANSLATION IS THE OBJECT'S WORLD POSITION: obj+0x26/+0x2a/+0x2e, which is what TargetSelect_CanTarget hands to Math_DistanceBetweenPoints, are this record's x/y/z.

fields.name: frameValid
fields.description: +0x32 -- clear means 'frame' has not been built from eulerAngles yet. Zeroed by SimObjectBase_Constructor; set to 1 by SimObject_InstallModelTransform and by Flyer_Constructor after it seeds the matrix itself.

fields.name: shapeInstance
fields.description: +0x34 -- the object's TSShapeInstance. Built by the root constructor from its second argument through FUN_00490a58, and tested and released by every deleting destructor in both hierarchies ('MOV ESI,dword ptr [EBX + 0x34]' in ProjectileBase_Dtor). Its per-node world transform array at shapeInstance+0x16 is what ShapeInst_BuildWorldTransforms fills.

fields.name: maybe_typeShapeRecord
fields.description: +0x41 -- a pointer into the class's own type table, stored by the shape layer of the constructor chain (0040332c, 00403368, 004033a4). A mech gets its HERCS.DAT row + 0xde. Distinct from the full type record each derived class stores for itself at +0x1f2.

fields.name: group
fields.description: +0x45 -- the mission group that placed this object. group+0x12 is the side byte every friend-or-foe test compares, and group+0x14 is the 'awaiting deployment' pointer Sim_DetectionTick skips on. Written by Mech_AttachToGroup (00417aa8) and Base_AttachToGroup (00405c3c).

fields.name: listIndex
fields.description: +0x4b -- the slot ObjectList_Add (00411dd4) put this object in, and the index that addresses a row of another object's 'contacts' and 'lineOfSightClear'. 'MOV DX,word ptr [EAX + 0x4b]' in Ai_KnowsObject settles the width.

fields.name: behaviour
fields.description: +0x4d -- the AI behaviour state, embedded rather than pointed to; it runs to +0x91, ending exactly where the flag block begins. See BehaviourBlock.

fields.name: radarVisible
fields.description: +0x95 -- set by Detection_Sweep (004128f8) when an active scanner on either side of a pair has line of sight, cleared wholesale by Detection_DecayContacts. A property of the object, unlike a contact, which is a property of a pair.

fields.name: scannerActive
fields.description: +0x96 -- this object's own active scanner. Toggled by Mech_ToggleRadarMode (0041b468); latched on by Base_Construct for structure types 5, 6, 0x1d and 0x1e. One of the two emissions the anti-radiation missile homes on.
+0x98 -- written to 1 by Mech_Constructor and Flyer_Constructor as '[EDI + 0x6]' off the 0x92 base, in the identical block all three constructors share. No reader located.

fields.name: destroyed
fields.description: +0x99 -- destroyed. Written only by the three classes' damage-write paths (Mech_ComponentDamageWrite when a core component reaches full damage, Flyer_ComponentDamageWrite, Base_ApplyDamage) and by Base_Construct for a structure spawned already destroyed. 'CMP byte ptr [EDX + 0x7],0x0' in TargetSelect_CanTarget (00433174) settles the width. The mech's writer also applies 30000 damage through vtable +0x74, clears scannerActive and fires the defeatAction.
+0x9a -- read by Ai_IsTargetable of the ASKING machine, gating a rejection of the object the cockpit view already holds. Meaning not established.

fields.name: engaged
fields.description: +0x9e -- 'this object has been closed with by an enemy that can see it'. Written to 1 by Detection_Sweep on both parties at once, alongside firing the engagement action.

fields.name: maybe_jammerActive
fields.description: +0xa1 -- the object's jammer, read by the anti-radiation missile's emission gate (Rocket_HomingSteer, 0040a254) and the ECM spoofing roll. Nothing in DBSIM has been seen to turn one on.

fields.name: perTickActionLatch
fields.description: +0xa2 -- cleared on every object by Sim_DetectionTick's third pass and tested before an engagement action fires, so it suppresses a second firing within a tick. That clear is the only writer located.

fields.name: locallyPiloted
fields.description: +0xa3 -- the machine the player is flying. Sim_DetectionTick holds it back to sweep LAST, after every other friendly object, so squadmates' contacts reach it first.

fields.name: immobilised
fields.description: +0xa4 -- this object can no longer move under its own power. Latched, never cleared. Mech_ComponentDamageWrite (00417de4) sets it when half or more of the legs have reached full damage, and Razor_MovementTick (004198f4) when the airframe loses its nose or belly -- for a flyer it is the harder stop, because the position integration refuses to run while it is set. Both writers also release the object's target and fire its defeatAction. NOT 'removed from the simulation'.

fields.name: disarmed
fields.description: +0xa5 -- this object has no working weapon. NOT a damage latch. Ai_ChooseWeapon (0041f358) latches it the first time it walks a machine's whole mount list and finds nothing, and fires the defeatAction on the way, which is the fourth of that action's four firing sites. A STRUCTURE IS BORN WITH IT: Base_Construct sets it for the ordinary-building vtable (00497940) and the radar-mast vtable (004979d4), and not for the three armed families (004978ac, 00497784, 00497818), so 'has no weapons' is the reading the structure branch confirms independently of the mech one.
+0xa7 -- written to 1 by Mech_Constructor and Flyer_Constructor as '[EAX + 0x15]' off the 0x92 base. No reader located.

fields.name: maybe_collapsed
fields.description: +0xb4 -- rejects a candidate in Ai_IsTargetable, separately from destroyed (+0x99) and invulnerable (+0xb7).

fields.name: invulnerable
fields.description: +0xb7 -- cannot be hurt at all, and outside the AI's candidate set entirely (Ai_IsTargetable). Only a structure sets it; Base_Construct latches it from BASES.DAT +0x1e.

fields.name: contacts
fields.description: +0xc2 -- one byte per object, indexed by the OTHER object's listIndex: 'iVar6 + 0xc2 + *(short *)(obj + 0x4b)' in TargetSelect_CanTarget. Filled by Detection_Sweep, emptied by Detection_DecayContacts. The length is the 0x70 gap to lineOfSightClear, corroborated by the identical 0x70 gap from there to targetedBy.

fields.name: lineOfSightClear
fields.description: +0x132 -- the same shape as 'contacts' and the same index: the cached answer to whether this object can see that one, rate-limited by sightCacheTimer. Detection_LineOfSight (00412608) is the only reader and writer.

fields.name: targetedBy
fields.description: +0x1a2 -- how many machines currently hold this object as their selected target. 'DEC word ptr [ECX + 0x1a2]' / 'INC word ptr [EAX + 0x1a2]' settles the width; every writer of a machine's target decrements the old one and increments the new.

fields.name: targetClass
fields.description: +0x1a8 -- what this object counts as when something decides whether to shoot it: -1 unclassified, 0 HERC, 1 structure, 2 flyer or ground vehicle, 3 emplacement. Every constructor writes 0xffff first and overwrites it, so an object that never finishes construction stays unclassified.

fields.name: engagementAction
fields.description: +0x1b2 -- the mission action this object fires when a hostile that already has contact on it closes to engagement range. Zeroed by all three constructors; set from the object's roster record.

fields.name: defeatAction
fields.description: +0x1b6 -- the mission action this object fires when it stops being a threat, which is how a retail mission chains its waves. NOT a death action: a machine that has run out of working weapons fires it too.
+0x1ba -- written to 0xffff by all three constructors ('MOV word ptr [EDX + 0x1ba],AX' in Base_Construct). Meaning not established.
+0x1bc -- written to 0xffff by all three constructors. Meaning not established.
+0x1be -- written to 0xffff by all three constructors. Meaning not established.

fields.name: sightCacheTimer
fields.description: +0x1e2 -- rate-limits lineOfSightClear. Ticked by Sim_DetectionTick's first pass through Math_CountdownTimerTick; reloaded with 5000 plus a roll of 1000 by Detection_LineOfSight.

fields.name: contactDecayTimer
fields.description: +0x1e5 -- the gap between passes of Detection_DecayContacts. On expiry Sim_DetectionTick reloads the counter at +0x1e6 with 10000 plus a roll of 1000 and runs the decay, so an object re-examines what it can see a few times a minute and the roll keeps a mission's objects off the same tick.

structs.name: ComponentDamageArrays
structs.description: The per-component damage header a machine keeps at mech+0x206. Three parallel arrays of accumulated damage plus the reference data they are read against; the arrays are heap blocks, the header is embedded. Allocated by Component_AllocDamageArrays (0040d2cc) with (29 components, 22 dependent subpieces) and wired up by Component_LinkMaxRefData (0040d354). Zero means undamaged, not destroyed -- these accumulate damage rather than hold remaining health.

fields.name: dependentDamage
fields.description: +0x00 -- the 22-entry dependent-subpiece damage array. Allocated as param_3*2 bytes and zeroed.

fields.name: componentDamage
fields.description: +0x04 -- the 29-entry main-component damage array. Allocated as param_2*2 bytes and zeroed.

fields.name: componentActive
fields.description: +0x08 -- the 29-entry active-flag array, memset to 0x01 rather than zeroed. This is the one Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage clears a slot in (docs write it as mech+0x20e[i] = 0) before writing the damage, so a destroyed mount stops being a target.

fields.name: maxRefData
fields.description: +0x0c -- the .DMG-derived per-component maximum/reference record, which is the mech's own mech+0x1fa handed in as Component_LinkMaxRefData's param_3. Mech_AiFleeCheck reads a component maximum through it.

fields.name: collisionRecord
fields.description: +0x10 -- the Collision_RegisterObject registration, the mech's own mech+0x1f6.

fields.name: owner
fields.description: +0x14 -- back-pointer to the object the header is embedded in.

fields.name: componentCount
fields.description: +0x18 -- Component_AllocDamageArrays stores its param_2 here; 29 for a mech.

fields.name: dependentCount
fields.description: +0x1a -- its param_3; 22 for a mech.

structs.name: ShieldBlock
structs.description: A machine's shield array: five shorts at mech+0x222, initialised by Shield_Init (00413a90) from the type record's +0xc0. There is one pool, not two -- max caps the SUM of the two facings and balance decides the split, which is why the manual can only say power is redistributed. docs/simulation/damage-system.md owns the recharge, absorb and balance-slew behaviour.

fields.name: front
fields.description: +0x00 -- front charge. Shield_Init seeds it to max>>1. Mech_GetShieldByHeading (004154d0) returns this facing within +/-90 degrees of the given heading.

fields.name: rear
fields.description: +0x02 -- rear charge, seeded the same way.

fields.name: balance
fields.description: +0x04 -- Q10 over 0-1024; Shield_Init writes 0x200, an even split.

fields.name: max
fields.description: +0x06 -- caps front + rear. Raised by a Shield Pod, so this is the live figure.

fields.name: baseMax
fields.description: +0x08 -- the type's capacity before any pod. Shield_Init writes the same value to both and nothing writes this one again.

structs.name: MechObject
structs.description: A HERC -- the class every walking machine and the RAZOR are instances of. Embeds SimObject at offset 0 (so the vtable, transform, behaviour block and flag block are the base's fields) and starts its own at +0x1f2, running to 0x36a. Constructed by Mech_Constructor (00415bb0), allocated from the pool set up at 00425185 whose element size is this struct's length.
notes: THE FLIGHT BLOCK AT +0x2b9 BELONGS TO THIS STRUCT, not to FlyerObject: a RAZOR is a mech with the type record's flyer flag set, which docs/simulation/razor-flight.md establishes and owns. The layout corroborates it -- +0x2b9 is past the end of the flyer class (0x291), and Mech_Constructor is what zeroes the block and seeds the airspeed.

THE TWO TIMER FLAVOURS ARE NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE FIELD, only from which function ticks it. +0x258 through +0x26c are seven 3-byte CountdownTimers stepped by Math_CountdownTimerTick; +0x26d through +0x280 are four 5-byte LongCountdownTimers stepped by Timer_CountDown. Both keep their counter at +1, which is why every doc cites these fields one byte above the record: mech+0x26b IS the counter of the timer based at +0x26a, not a field of its own. Searching for the cited offset finds the accesses; searching for it as a record base finds nothing.

+0x261 IS A LOCK TIMER SLOT THAT NOTHING TICKS. The run from +0x258 has a regular stride of 3 and +0x264 is the fifth element of it, so the fourth exists in the layout; no call to Math_CountdownTimerTick names it, matching the engine port's note that missile subtype 3 is never used.

THE GAPS AT +0x1fe, +0x24c, +0x2a4 AND +0x301 ARE UNREAD, NOT ESTABLISHED AS PADDING. No access to them was located; they are left out rather than filled so a later finding does not have to displace an invented field.

THE EXTENT OF +0x240 IS DERIVED, NOT READ. Ai_DriveToPoint takes it as a point pointer and every other world point in this struct is three int32s, but +0x248 holds an object pointer, so it cannot run past +0x247. Recorded as two int32s on that ground alone.

fields.name: base
fields.description: +0x00 -- the base class, embedded. Field 0 of it is the vtable, which Mech_Constructor points at MechVtable (0049a282).

fields.name: typeRecord
fields.description: +0x1f2 -- this chassis' 0x21e-byte type record, indexed out of DAT_004a9de8 by Mech_Constructor. Read by nearly every mech method for the chassis figures.

fields.name: collisionModel
fields.description: +0x1f6 -- the Collision_RegisterObject registration for the type's .COL file.

fields.name: damageRecord
fields.description: +0x1fa -- the type's .DMG file, loaded by Damage_LoadMechDmgFile. Handed straight to Component_LinkMaxRefData, so it is also componentDamage.maxRefData.

fields.name: weaponMounts
fields.description: +0x202 -- the weapon-mount manager. Its +0x04 is the mount array and +0x08 the count, which is how Mech_ComputeCombatRating walks the machine's hardpoints.

fields.name: componentDamage
fields.description: +0x206 -- allocated in place by Component_AllocDamageArrays(mech+0x206, 0x1d, 0x16).

fields.name: shield
fields.description: +0x222 -- Shield_Init(mech+0x222, typeRecord+0xc0).

fields.name: locomotionThread
fields.description: +0x22c -- the animation thread the walk cycle is seeked on, built from typeRecord+0x12, or null when the chassis has no such sequence. Mech_LocomotionTick drives it.

fields.name: turretTwistThread
fields.description: +0x230 -- the same for the torso twist, from typeRecord+0x1c.

fields.name: turretPitchThread
fields.description: +0x234 -- and the pitch, from typeRecord+0x24.

fields.name: parts
fields.description: +0x238 -- a malloc'd array of pointers to the machine's own child objects, one per entry in the type record's list at +0x72. Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround walks it to place the legs.

fields.name: partCount
fields.description: +0x23c -- how many, counted by Mech_Constructor off the same list.

fields.name: squadOrderVerb
fields.description: +0x23e -- the standing squad order, 0 for none. Verb 4 is engage, and Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder (0041c478) clears it when its target is let go.

fields.name: squadOrderDestination
fields.description: +0x240 -- where a standing squad order sends the machine; Ai_NavigationStep hands it to Ai_DriveToPoint. See the note on its extent.

fields.name: squadOrderTarget
fields.description: +0x248 -- the order's target object, compared against the selected target at +0x1a4 by Ai_ClearSquadEngageOrder.

fields.name: squadOrderAbandonTier
fields.description: +0x250 -- how finished the order wants its target before the machine may drop it. Ai_ShouldAbandonTarget (0041c4a8) compares Ai_TargetStateTier against it.

fields.name: cruiseSpeed
fields.description: +0x252 -- the speed Ai_DriveToPoint walks at, out of the mission file. Zero means the 0xaa default, which is what 91% of retail records carry.

fields.name: avoidanceBias
fields.description: +0x254 -- +/-5000, picked by a coin flip when the machine gets stuck, biasing obstacle avoidance to one side for as long as unstickTimer runs.

fields.name: reactorRate
fields.description: +0x256 -- the reactor's output rate, which Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate runs through Math_IntegrateRateOverTick into the energy pool. The reactor is a rate; the pool is a capacitor.

fields.name: lockTimer0
fields.description: +0x258 -- missile-subtype 0's lock countdown, ticked by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate through Math_CountdownTimerTick(mech + 600).

fields.name: lockTimer1
fields.description: +0x25b -- subtype 1.

fields.name: lockTimer2
fields.description: +0x25e -- subtype 2.
+0x261 -- subtype 3's slot. Placed on the run's stride rather than on an access; see the note.

fields.name: lockTimer4
fields.description: +0x264 -- subtype 4.

fields.name: ecmRollTimer
fields.description: +0x267 -- the gap between ECM spoof rolls against a jamming target. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate reloads the counter at +0x268 with 5000 after a roll that spoofed and 0x5dc after one that did not.

fields.name: radarSilenceTimer
fields.description: +0x26a -- how long the radar is held off. Mech_DirectFireHitTest loads 6000 into the counter at +0x26b on an anti-radiation missile hit, and that is the ARM working: the machine goes dark long enough for a seeker to lose it.

fields.name: unstickTimer
fields.description: +0x26d -- the post-collision back-off. Mech_MovementTick loads 10000 into the counter at +0x26e, and while it runs the machine ignores its desired speed and drives at the chassis maximum, avoidanceBias deciding which way.

fields.name: retargetCooldown
fields.description: +0x272 -- Mech_AiOnTakingFire loads 10000 into +0x273, which is what stops a machine under sustained fire from re-picking a target every tick.

fields.name: friendlyFireComplaintCooldown
fields.description: +0x277 -- the gap between friendly-fire callouts; counter at +0x278.

fields.name: underFireWindow
fields.description: +0x27c -- Mech_AiOnTakingFire loads 30000 into +0x27d. Its expiry is what clears damageFromPlayerGroup.

fields.name: damageFromPlayerGroup
fields.description: +0x281 -- damage taken from the player's own group inside underFireWindow, summed by Mech_AiOnTakingFire and tested against 8000. Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate zeroes it.
+0x285 -- ticked by Mech_PerTickSystemsUpdate, which reloads the counter at +0x286 with 4000. What it gates is not established.

fields.name: damageTaken
fields.description: +0x288 -- the running total of damage this machine has taken. Mech_DirectFireHitTest adds to it; the AI's circling step spends it, breaking off only past 100.

fields.name: turnRate
fields.description: +0x28c -- binary angle per tick, added straight to the heading by Mech_LocomotionTick. There is no velocity vector anywhere in this struct: movement is animation root motion.

fields.name: speed
fields.description: +0x28e -- the walker speed scalar, which scales the animation rather than integrating a position. Never written on a flight path; Mech_GetSpeed returns Q10(2000, this) for a walker.

fields.name: throttle
fields.description: +0x290 -- throttle setting, Q10 over +/-0x400, its sign the direction of travel. Written by Mech_ApplyThrottleInput and, when the cockpit gauge is being dragged, by Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate.

fields.name: energyPool
fields.description: +0x292 -- the Master Energy Pool. Mech_Constructor seeds 10000 and the tick clamps back to it; every consumer draws on this, never on the reactor.

fields.name: turretTwistRate
fields.description: +0x294 -- binary angle per second, built up toward what the stick asks for.

fields.name: turretPitchRate
fields.description: +0x296 -- the pitch counterpart.

fields.name: turretTwist
fields.description: +0x298 -- the turret's twist angle relative to the machine's own heading. Mech vtable +0x3c returns it, and the front window's Rotation Indicator reads it exactly.

fields.name: turretPitch
fields.description: +0x29a -- positive looks up.
+0x29c -- zeroed by Mech_Constructor. No other access located.

fields.name: combatRating
fields.description: +0x29e -- what this machine is worth as a target and how willing it is to fight, computed by Mech_ComputeCombatRating (0041edd8) and cached behind the +0x94 dirty flag. It falls as the machine is shot apart.

fields.name: animationRate
fields.description: +0x2a0 -- animation playback rate. In steady state it equals speed; Mech_MovementTick negates it and Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround reads its sign to tell walking from reversing.

fields.name: aimComponentSlot
fields.description: +0x2a2 -- the component slot the machine is working at, or -1. Written by Mech_AiSelectAimComponent (0041ce08); Mech_AiCombatReassess resets it to -1.

fields.name: fear
fields.description: +0x2aa -- 0 at construction, then 1000, 600 or 300 as Mech_AiFleeCheck (0041cb94) raises it. Mapped through [0, 1024] -> [150, -100] it becomes Ai_ChooseWeapon's score floor, so a frightened machine fires almost anything it has left.

fields.name: latchedMount
fields.description: +0x2ac -- the weapon mount held across ticks. Only an ELF is ever kept, which is what lets an AI machine sustain a burst instead of re-rolling its choice; Ai_FireAtPoint (0041f5a0) clears it as soon as the mount stops being ready or in range.

fields.name: collisionLockCandidate
fields.description: +0x2b0 -- a structure recorded as a lock-on candidate by Mech_CollisionTest, separately from its block test. Only the behaviour layer reads it.

fields.name: legArmed
fields.description: +0x2b4 -- one arming byte a leg. Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround takes this as a char cursor and walks it alongside the parts array; a foot swings forward past the arming figure and plants as it comes back through the trigger.

+0x2b8 -- the arming byte Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround switches its cursor to for the part matching the type record's +0x46, so it is a fifth arming flag outside the leg run rather than part of it. Mech_Constructor seeds it to 1 where the four legs get 0.

fields.name: bodyVelocity
fields.description: +0x2b9 -- velocity in the airframe's own frame: X sideslip (-X is port), Y airspeed, Z vertical. Mech_Constructor zeroes 0x4e bytes from here, which is the whole flight block, and seeds the Y component to 1000.

fields.name: worldVelocity
fields.description: +0x2c5 -- the same velocity in world space, and what Razor_MovementTick integrates into the position.

fields.name: pitchRate
fields.description: +0x2d1 -- binary angle per unit time.

fields.name: yawRate
fields.description: +0x2d5 -- what the rudder builds, distinct from the heading rate the bank produces.

fields.name: flyerThrottle
fields.description: +0x2d7 -- the flyer's own throttle, a second copy of throttle rather than the same field. Razor_ApplyFlightInput copies it onto +0x290 and sets the +0x93 dirty flag, and Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate writes both under the type record's flyer flag -- which is the only path by which the cockpit slider reaches a RAZOR.

fields.name: eulerAnglesPtr
fields.description: +0x2d9 -- back-pointer to the object's own euler triple at +0x0c, set by Mech_Constructor. Every flight path addresses the block through it.

fields.name: previousFrameInverse
fields.description: +0x2dd -- last tick's transform, transposed and with the translation negated and rotated. Mech_Constructor builds it from +0x12 and +0x26 and then inverts it in place; the docs cite +0x2f1 separately, which is this transform's own translation.

fields.name: bankHeadingRate
fields.description: +0x2fd -- the heading rate the current bank angle is producing. This is what turns a RAZOR: there is no rudder-driven yaw in the heading.

fields.name: equipmentPods
fields.description: +0x307 -- ECM, targeting computer, Shield Pod, Energy Pod, Turbo Pod, in that slot order. MechLoadout_FileEquipmentPods (0040fb2c) memsets 0x14 bytes and files five specific catalog ids out of the finished mount list, so a slot is null unless that pod is fitted.

fields.name: attWaitTimer
fields.description: +0x31c -- how long Automatic Turret Tracking waits with the latch on and nothing selected. Player_PerFrameCockpitUpdate arms it with 0x1194.

fields.name: blockedLineOfFirePoint
fields.description: +0x31e -- where the machine last had its line of fire blocked. Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked (0041dd2c) copies the target's position here and sets +0xad; Mech_BehaviourSkirtThink then walks an arc around it.

applications.description: TargetSelect_CanTarget's candidate. Parameter 0 is the asking object but one branch replaces it with a global, so it is not typed.
Ai_IsTargetable's asking machine -- reads +0x45, the 0x92 flag block and +0x1a8 off it.
Ai_KnowsObject's candidate -- the object whose listIndex indexes the asker's contact row.
Mech_Constructor's object. It is the widest single reader of this struct: it writes the type record, both sub-object headers, the animation threads, the parts array, the flight block and the pods.
Mech_ApplyThrottleInput's machine. Declared 'int param_1' by the decompiler, so its field offsets read as byte displacements already.
Mech_PlaceLegsOnGround's machine -- walks parts/partCount against legArmed.
Mech_GetSpeed's machine. Mech vtable +0x38; branches on the type record's flyer flag between bodyVelocity[1] and speed.
Mech_AiFleeCheck's machine -- the sole writer of fear.
Mech_ComputeCombatRating's machine -- the sole writer of combatRating.
Mech_AiSelectAimComponent's machine -- the sole writer of aimComponentSlot.
Ai_DriveToPoint's machine. Parameter 1 is a bare world point, not an object.
Ai_FireAtPoint's machine -- reads and clears latchedMount.
Ai_UpdateWeaponsFree's machine -- the AI's radar switch.
Mech_AiOnTakingFire's machine. Mech vtable slot; loads retargetCooldown and underFireWindow.
Mech_DirectFireHitTest's struck machine. Mech vtable slot.
Mech_ApplyDirectFireDamage's struck machine. Mech vtable slot.
Mech_GetShieldByHeading's machine. Mech vtable +0x34; returns shield.front or shield.rear.
Mech_CompareCombatRating's asking machine. Mech vtable +0x4c. Its candidate is left untyped: the function returns 0 for every non-HERC, so the parameter is not a mech.
Mech_AiOnLineOfFireBlocked's machine. Mech vtable +0x64; the sole writer of blockedLineOfFirePoint.
Component_AllocDamageArrays' header -- the one place the three array pointers and the two counts are written.
Component_LinkMaxRefData's header -- writes the three reference fields at +0x0c, +0x10 and +0x14.
